assays.assay_name: Cued Pavlovian Fear Conditioning (Acquisition, Extinction, Recall)
assays.assay_description: Standard fear conditioning chambers (Maze Engineers); acquisition (Context A): 4 min baseline + 8 CS-US pairings (30 s 1000 Hz tone co-terminating with 0.4 mA, 2 s footshock) + 1 min; extinction & recall (Context B): 4 min baseline + 12 CS-only trials + 1 min. Freezing scored automatically with Any-maze. Conducted in stress-naive, SPS, and CRS cohorts at 1 and 3 mg/kg psilocybin or saline given 30 min before extinction.

application_type.evidence: received their assigned drug treatment ... via intraperitoneal (IP) injection, 30 min prior to fear extinction training

setup_habituation.evidence: No apparatus habituation described prior to acquisition.

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were freely moving in fear conditioning chambers; freezing scored via Any-maze video tracking.

food_restriction.evidence: No food access mentioned in the fear conditioning chamber during testing.

water_restriction.evidence: No water access mentioned in the fear conditioning chamber during testing.

time_to_assay.evidence: received their assigned drug treatment ... 30 min prior to fear extinction training

sample_size.evidence: Behavioral data: saline n = 30, psilocybin 3 mg/kg n = 24, psilocybin 1 mg/kg n = 10; SPS and CRS behavioral data: n = 12 per group

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin (3 mg/kg, i.p.) administered 30 min before extinction enhanced cued fear extinction and reduced freezing during extinction recall 24 h later in stress-naive mice; 1 mg/kg had no significant effect on extinction but reduced recall freezing. Psilocybin produced similar enhancement of extinction and recall in SPS- and CRS-stressed animals, rescuing stress-induced extinction deficits despite blunted HPA axis responsivity in stressed groups.
outcomes.statistics: Extinction (naive): time x treatment F(11,539)=2.738, p=0.0019; treatment F(5.063,248.1)=66.73, p=0.0152. Recall (naive): time x treatment F(22,638)=2.747, p<0.0001. SPS extinction: F(11,198)=2.869, p=0.0016; treatment F(1,18)=5.832, p=0.0266. SPS recall: treatment F(1,18)=11.99, p=0.0028. CRS extinction: F(11,242)=2.737, p=0.0024. CRS recall: F(5.803,127.7)=1.865, p=0.0942.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin-treated (3 mg/kg) animals displayed enhanced fear extinction compared to their saline-treated counterparts ... animals that had received either dose of psilocybin prior to extinction displayed reduced freezing during recall compared to their saline counterparts

judge_notes: All three candidates identified a single fear conditioning assay; consolidated as one assay covering acquisition, extinction, and recall phases across stress-naive, SPS, and CRS cohorts per rubric (different phases and stress cohorts = 1 assay).
B1 scored 0 (single measure: % freezing) following majority of candidates; glm's score of 1 was inconsistent with its own evidence stating only freezing was measured.
D4 scored 0: acquisition is in a different context from extinction/recall, and no pre-drug baseline data within the extinction context were reported.
Vehicle scored 'saline' based on paper's saline control group description.
Housing handling and enrichment marked not_reported (low confidence) as paper is silent on these.
